findings.title: `unsubscribe` dereferences a `TopicUser` that `find_by` may return as nil
findings.description: The new action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. A logged-in user who has never interacted with the topic has no `TopicUser` row, so `find_by` returns nil and the action raises `NoMethodError` (a 500). The fix is to use `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(...)` or to handle the nil case explicitly before the comparison.

findings.title: Topic title is rendered with triple-stash inside the unsubscribe template
findings.description: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML. The controller interpolates `model.fancyTitle` into that string. This is only safe if `fancyTitle` is already HTML-escaped on the server, which I could not confirm from the diff. Confirm that `fancy_title` escapes its input, or switch to double-stash and avoid HTML in the i18n string.
